The leading digit is $a_N(x)=x-1006$, so $a_N(0)=-1006$.

**Degree of the leading term.** Each term $a_k b^k$ has degree at most $2k+1$. The left side has degree 2015, so $2N+\deg a_N=2015$. Since $\deg a_N\le 1$, this forces $N=1007$ and $\deg a_N=1$.

**Isolating $a_N$.** Every lower term $a_k b^k$ with $k<N$ has degree at most $2N-1$. Dividing by $b^N$, which has degree $2N$, gives terms of negative degree. So $a_N$ is the polynomial part of $S/b^{N}$, where
$$S=\frac{x^{2016}-1}{x-1}.$$

**Expansion at infinity.** Let $u=1/x$. The "$-1$" in the numerator only affects very low-order terms, so
$$\frac{S}{b^{1007}}=\frac{x^{2015}\,(1-u)^{-1}\,(1-u^{2016})}{x^{2014}(1+u+u^2)^{1007}}=x\cdot\frac{1}{(1-u)(1+u+u^2)^{1007}}+\cdots$$

The coefficient of $u$ in $\dfrac{1}{(1-u)(1+u+u^2)^{1007}}$ is $1-1007=-1006$. The polynomial part is therefore $x-1006$.

ANSWER: -1006
